chat.text: I think the open question is not "How do we profile down CMS?" -- we think that problem is easy. The open question is "What happens in 10 years when you're trying to get keys off an unpatched HSM and to do that you need to present it attestation for the new HSM that it's importing into, and CMS has invented new SignerInfo extensions in that time".

chat.author: Jon Geater
chat.text:
Strictly adding attributes and encodings and not removing any is fine: an old key with a small number of attributes will still work on an old or new recipient. A new key with more attriibutes will work on a new recipient. The only issue is a new key on an old recipient...in which case, abort.
This seems completely reasonable to me, since the old recipient will also not honour the meaning of the thing it doesn't understand, and every attribute has to be considered important. Making them ignorable is very dangerous

chat.author: Mike Ounsworth
chat.text: Carsten, that's probably the right terminology here: Is CMS forwards compatible, and / or can we define a CMS profile that's guaranteed to be forwards compatible. That's a really good phrasing of the core question here.

chat.author: Mike Ounsworth
chat.text:
Ned Smith said:

@Mike a level of transparency could be a claim

I think my point is more that you can have Level 3: Public Source Code even if you don't have Level 1: Public Binary because you yourself don't provide a build.
And Level 5: Formal Verification of source code could be done even on closed source, pay-for-binary applications. So these seem like useful properties to be able to attest, but to me they don't seem like a linear ordering where Level 4 implies Levels 1 -> 3.

chat.author: Ned Smith
